channel.title: HAX Element Schema

item.title: Overview
item.description: HAXElementSchema is the lightweight object format HAX uses as a virtual DOM representation before converting to real DOM nodes. This is a companion spec to hax-schema . Where hax-schema explains the full haxProperties contract for element authoring, this site focuses specifically on the element payload objects used in demoSchema , insertion, and conversion workflows. item.title: Virtual DOM Usage Points
item.description: HAX uses the HAXElementSchema object shape as a lightweight virtual DOM payload during authoring operations. The object is passed around, transformed, and only materialized into actual nodes at insertion/render time. These are the primary usage points in HAX core: Virtual DOM → DOM conversion haxElementToNode(haxSchema) creates real nodes from tag , properties , and content . item.title: Runtime Behavior & JSON Schema
item.description: Runtime conversion behavior In HAX core, conversion happens primarily in two functions: haxElementToNode(haxSchema) — converts a schema object to a real DOM node. nodeToHaxElement(node, eventName) — converts a DOM node to a schema object. Important behavior to be aware of: Camel-cased property keys are converted to dash-cased attributes where needed. true sets boolean attributes, false removes them.
